sentences.en: Well, two big things, I guess.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想主要是两件大事。

sentences.en: First is that we voted SENDERS, the C++ Asynchrony Framework, into C++26.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们把 C++ 异步框架 SENDERS 投票纳入了 C++26。

sentences.en: And the second is that we design-approved reflection for C++26.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，我们为 C++26 的反射设计方案投了赞成票。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 189, recorded on July 3rd, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 189 期，录制于 2024 年 7 月 3 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we chat about the ISO C++ committee meeting that just took place in St. Louis,
sentences.zh: 我是康纳（Connor），今天我和我的联合主持人布莱斯（Bryce）一起聊聊刚刚在圣路易斯召开的 ISO C++ 委员会会议，

sentences.en: as well as our upcoming conference trip to CPP North.
sentences.zh: 以及我们即将前往北方 C++ 大会（CPP North）的行程。

sentences.en: Look at that view, folks.
sentences.zh: 大家看那个风景。

sentences.en: You had a nice view before, but it's even better now.
sentences.zh: 你之前视野就不错，现在更棒了。

sentences.en: Yes, and in fact, I've been working hard to figure out how to position my desk in this room so that I can show off the beautiful view of Manhattan and also not have my screen be,
sentences.zh: 是的，事实上我一直在努力研究怎么在这个房间里摆放书桌，这样既能展现曼哈顿的美丽景色，又不会让我的屏幕……

sentences.en: like, super backlit.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，背光太强。

sentences.en: But there's just really no option for not having a backlit screen here unless I, like, go in the closet.
sentences.zh: 但这里实在没有办法避免屏幕背光，除非我……比如钻到壁橱里去。

sentences.en: Well, it's been a while since we've chatted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们好久没聊天了。

sentences.en: How did the move go?
sentences.zh: 搬家怎么样？

sentences.en: How is the new place?
sentences.zh: 新地方怎么样？

sentences.en: How's the view?
sentences.zh: 风景怎么样？

sentences.en: The view does look fantastic, folks.
sentences.zh: 风景看起来确实棒极了，各位。

sentences.en: You'll have to post a photo for the people, for the listeners.
sentences.zh: 你得为观众、为听众们发张照片。

sentences.en: The move is going well.
sentences.zh: 搬家挺顺利的。

sentences.en: Going?
sentences.zh: 还在搬？

sentences.en: It's still going?
sentences.zh: 还在搬吗？

sentences.en: We talked, like, a month ago.
sentences.zh: 我们大概一个月前才聊过。

sentences.en: No, we moved in a week before the C++ St. Louis committee meeting, and so we were here for, like, six days.
sentences.zh: 不，我们在 C++ 圣路易斯委员会会议前一周搬进来的，所以我们在这里呆了大概六天。

sentences.en: And then I went to the St. Louis committee meeting, and then my girlfriend went to Florida, to where my parents are, to go to play at a tennis academy there.
sentences.zh: 然后我去参加了圣路易斯委员会会议，接着我女朋友去了佛罗里达我父母那里，去那里的网球学院打球。

sentences.en: Ooh, fancy.
sentences.zh: 哦，真高级。

sentences.en: I told her that, look, we're both very territorial people, and this new apartment needs to be, like, a shared space.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她，听着，我们俩领地意识都很强，这个新公寓必须是一个共享空间。

sentences.en: And if one of us is in this new apartment for, like, a week right after we moved in without the other one, we're going to make all sorts of executive decisions,
sentences.zh: 如果刚搬进来后，我们俩中有一个人在没有另一个人的情况下在这个新公寓里呆上大约一周，我们就会做出各种各样的独断决定，

sentences.en: and the other person's going to come back.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个人回来时。

sentences.en: And there's going to be no reversing those executive decisions.
sentences.zh: 那些独断的决定就无法撤销了。

sentences.en: So I said, either you've got to come with me to St. Louis, I've got to not go to St. Louis, or you've got to go somewhere else and do something else.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，要么你跟我去圣路易斯，要么我不去圣路易斯，要么你去别的地方做别的事。

sentences.en: And she picked the last option.
sentences.zh: 她选了最后一种。

sentences.en: But a couple of slight issues.
sentences.zh: 不过出了点小问题。

sentences.en: Two of the AC units in the apartment were dead on arrival.
sentences.zh: 公寓里的两个空调一到货就是坏的。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不是吧。

sentences.en: But the landlord's been very good about getting people out to fix them.
sentences.zh: 但房东很好，派了人来修。

sentences.en: But the AC people came right before I was going to leave for my flight.
sentences.zh: 不过修空调的人在我准备去赶飞机前刚好赶到。

sentences.en: This is to St. Louis, I assume?
sentences.zh: 我猜这是去圣路易斯？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, to St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 对，对，去圣路易斯。

sentences.en: And they – the circuit breaker box in this apartment was apparently not labeled correctly when they first put it in there because the AC people accidentally turned off the fridge.
sentences.zh: 然后他们——这个公寓的断路器箱刚装好时显然标签贴错了，因为修空调的人不小心把冰箱给关了。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不会吧。

sentences.en: And we came back, and everything in the fridge was spoiled rotten.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来时，冰箱里的所有东西都烂透了。

sentences.en: So we came back to no AC and also a slightly stinky apartment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们回来时不仅没有空调，公寓里还有点发臭。

sentences.en: Well, not slightly stinky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不只是有点臭。

sentences.en: It was fairly stinky.
sentences.zh: 简直相当臭。

sentences.en: And actually, we were both supposed to fly back at the same time on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，我们本该在周日同一时间飞回来。

sentences.en: I was going to get into LaGuardia at like 2.30 on Sunday, and my girlfriend was going to land at like 3.30.
sentences.zh: 我本打算在周日大约 2:30 到达拉瓜迪亚机场，我女朋友大概 3:30 降落。

sentences.en: But there were thunderstorms in New York and in Florida.
sentences.zh: 但纽约和佛罗里达都有雷暴。

sentences.en: And so she ended up being at the airport for like five or six hours on Sunday because it kept being like, oh, we can't leave because there's thunderstorm over Tampa.
sentences.zh: 所以她最后在机场待了大概五六个小时，因为周日一直收到通知说，哦，我们不能走，因为坦帕上空有雷暴。

sentences.en: And then when it was clear over Tampa, there would be a thunderstorm in New York, and they wouldn't be able to leave and get to New York.
sentences.zh: 然后当坦帕上空放晴时，纽约又有了雷暴，他们就无法起飞前往纽约。

sentences.en: And then it just like flipped back and forth all day, and then eventually they were just like, all right, everybody go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 接着这种情况整整一天反复横跳，最后他们终于说，好了，大家都去睡觉吧。

sentences.en: We're going to fly out the next morning.
sentences.zh: 我们明天早上再飞。

sentences.en: And in hindsight, it was good that this happened because if we had both arrived home at the same time and she had had to smell what I smelled, she would not have been happy,
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，发生这事倒挺庆幸的，因为如果我们俩同时到家，而她闻到了我闻到的味道，她绝不会高兴，

sentences.en: and she would have never used that fridge again.
sentences.zh: 而且她也绝对不会再用那个冰箱了。

sentences.en: We would have just had to buy a new fridge.
sentences.zh: 我们就只能买个新冰箱了。

sentences.en: That is still a possibility that we may never get the ick out of the fridge.
sentences.zh: 不过我们可能永远也去不掉冰箱里的那股怪味，这种可能性依然存在。

sentences.en: And then continuing the series of unfortunate events, I tried to upgrade CMake on my workstation, which is in Santa Clara yesterday.
sentences.zh: 接着这一连串倒霉事还没完，昨天我试图升级我位于圣克拉拉的工作站上的 CMake。

sentences.en: And Debian wanted to install a new LibC, and LibC wanted to run this user merge thing.
sentences.zh: 结果 Debian 想要安装一个新的 LibC，而 LibC 又要运行这个用户合并的东西。

sentences.en: And long story short, my workstation is like completely bricked.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，我的工作站彻底瘫痪变砖了。

sentences.en: My dynamic linker, which is a thing that every program needs to run, somehow got overwritten.
sentences.zh: 我的动态链接器，也就是每个程序运行都必需的东西，不知怎么被覆盖了。

sentences.en: The sim link to it got overwritten.
sentences.zh: 指向它的符号链接被覆盖了。

sentences.en: And then I couldn't run anything.
sentences.zh: 然后我就什么也运行不了了。

sentences.en: And I could have gotten myself out of this hole because I still had an SSH session into the machine, but I was not SSHed in as root.
sentences.zh: 我本可以脱离困境，因为我还有一个连到这台机器的 SSH 会话，但我登录 SSH 时不是 root 用户。

sentences.en: So I eventually could invoke the command that would create the sim link I needed to restore the system,
sentences.zh: 所以我最终能够调用创建恢复系统所需符号链接的命令，

sentences.en: but I didn't have root access and I needed it to be able to create that sim link.
sentences.zh: 但我没有 root 权限，而创建符号链接需要这个权限。

sentences.en: And so I had a very diligent coworker who was able to go over to the system and live boot it with a live USB and create the sim link.
sentences.zh: 于是我有一个非常勤奋的同事，他跑到系统旁边，用 Live USB 进行现场引导并创建了符号链接。

sentences.en: But as he's live booting, he's like, you know, this machine's running really hot.
sentences.zh: 但在他现场引导时，他说，你知道吗，这台机器运行得太热了。

sentences.en: I think your water cooler is dead.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的水冷坏了。

sentences.en: So then he goes to Ichi to try to find a water cooler and they don't have a new cooler.
sentences.zh: 于是他去秋叶原（Ichi）试图找一个水冷，但他们没有新散热器。

sentences.en: So then eventually he goes and like cannibalizes another system, finally finds a cooler that's like going to work for my system, gets my system back up.
sentences.zh: 所以最后他去拆了另一个系统的零件，终于找到了一个能适合我系统的散热器，把我的系统重新启动了。

sentences.en: But I still can't actually get into it.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上还是进不去。

sentences.en: It is like up and running now, but there seems to be some other issue.
sentences.zh: 它现在虽然启动并运行了，但似乎还有其他问题。

sentences.en: So it's just not been my week, man.
sentences.zh: 所以这真不是我的周啊，老兄。

sentences.en: There seems to be a theme, AC, fridge, and cooling system.
sentences.zh: 似乎有个主题：空调、冰箱和冷却系统。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: No, I can't even think about that.
sentences.zh: 不，我甚至都不想去想这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Everything to do with the temperature is broken.
sentences.zh: 所有跟温度有关的东西都坏了。

sentences.en: So what percentage are you moved?
sentences.zh: 所以你们搬了多少百分比了？

sentences.en: Are you fully moved in?
sentences.zh: 完全搬进去了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, all of our stuff is here.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们所有的东西都在这儿了。

sentences.en: I mean, my room is unpacked.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的房间已经收拾好了。

sentences.en: Is this a webcam?
sentences.zh: 这是网络摄像头吗？

sentences.en: Can you pick it up and rotate it around?
sentences.zh: 你能把它拿起来转一圈吗？

sentences.en: It is attached here.
sentences.zh: 它是固定在这里的。

sentences.en: However, I do have controls.
sentences.zh: 不过，我有控制权。

sentences.en: So I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我做不到那个。

sentences.en: This is the second bedroom, which is where my office is.
sentences.zh: 这是第二个卧室，也就是我的办公室。

sentences.en: You can see it's not fully unpacked.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它还没有完全收拾好。

sentences.en: Oh, and it does have, it does do 360.
sentences.zh: 哦，它确实有，它确实能 360 度旋转。

sentences.en: No, maybe it doesn't go 360.
sentences.zh: 不对，也许不能 360 度旋转。

sentences.en: It's called the Insta360.
sentences.zh: 它叫 Insta360。

sentences.en: So I would have assumed it would go all the way around.
sentences.zh: 所以我本以为它能转一整圈。

sentences.en: But I guess it gives you 360 degrees, but does not actually rotate all the way around, which kind of makes sense.
sentences.zh: 但我想它提供的是 360 度的视角，但实际上并不能转整整一圈，这倒也说得通。

sentences.en: Is this a new camera?
sentences.zh: 这是新相机吗？

sentences.en: I've never seen you in such high fidelity slash you've never been able to spin your camera around like that before.
sentences.zh: 我从来没见你这么高清过，或者说你以前从来没法像这样转动摄像头。

sentences.en: The camera, there was no way to set the contraSt.
sentences.zh: 这个相机，以前没法调节对比度。

sentences.en: And there was no positioning of the camera where either my face would be very dark or it would be like very backlit.
sentences.zh: 无论摄像头怎么摆放，要么我的脸很黑，要么背光非常严重。

sentences.en: And so I needed to get something where I had contrast control.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要买一个能控制对比度的设备。

sentences.en: And so I got this thing.
sentences.zh: 于是我买了这个东西。

sentences.en: It also has like some AI and tracking.
sentences.zh: 它还有一些人工智能和追踪功能。

sentences.en: And then, oh, the most exciting thing is this building doesn't have a gym, which I was able to use as justification to put in this bad boy.
sentences.zh: 然后，哦，最令人兴奋的是这栋楼没有健身房，我正好以此为借口把这个好宝贝给搬进来了。

sentences.en: Anyway, a Bowflex Max 10, Max 16 elliptical slash stair machine, which is very good, far better than the ellipticals in my old building.
sentences.zh: 总之，这是一台 Bowflex Max 10、Max 16 椭圆机兼楼梯机，非常好，远比我旧大楼里的椭圆机好得多。

sentences.en: I mean, I got quite the workout last night.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我昨晚进行了相当不错的锻炼。

sentences.en: That's quite nice because then if you're in a meeting, I've always kind of wanted that.
sentences.zh: 那挺不错的，这样如果你在开会的话——我一直挺想要这个的。

sentences.en: Like if you're in a meeting, you can just like, you know, do some stairs while you're right at your computer, basically.
sentences.zh: 比如你在开会时，基本上就可以一边爬楼梯，一边就在电脑前工作。

sentences.en: That was a big part of the motivation is that this unlocks like an extra two to three hours of meetings for me.
sentences.zh: 这就是很大一部分动力所在，因为这为我额外腾出了两到三个小时的开会时间。

sentences.en: Because it's hard to do meetings in the gym because it would be rude.
sentences.zh: 因为在健身房里开会很难，那样很不礼貌。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I still like to get out on my bike and actually like go out and ride.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我还是喜欢骑着自行车出去真正骑行。

sentences.en: But especially during the winter, this thing's going to be clutch for multitasking.
sentences.zh: 但特别是冬天的时候，这东西对于多任务处理简直是神器。

sentences.en: So if I'm out of breath during a meeting, it's probably because I'm on this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以在开会时如果我上气不接下气，那可能就是因为我在用这玩意儿。

sentences.en: I think it's an entire – in 2024, it's an entirely reasonable and like it should be encouraged almoSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这完全——在 2024 年，这完全合理，甚至可以说是应该受到鼓励的。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's some study out there that shows exercise elevates brain activity and, you know, mental focus.
sentences.zh: 我确信有些研究表明运动能提高大脑活动和（你知道的）精神专注力。

sentences.en: And I've heard people on meetings before that they definitely sound like they're on a walk or they're doing some exercise.
sentences.zh: 我以前听别人开会时，听得出来他们绝对是在散步或者在做某种运动。

sentences.en: But like isn't that – that's what Steve Jobs used to do, you know.
sentences.zh: 但这不是——史蒂夫·乔布斯以前就是这么干的，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, we're doing a meeting.
sentences.zh: 就像，哦，我们要开会了。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 走吧。

sentences.en: We're out the door.
sentences.zh: 我们出门。

sentences.en: We're going for a walk around Cupertino.
sentences.zh: 我们要去库比蒂诺散步。

sentences.en: And I think it's good, you know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺好的，你知道。

sentences.en: And I think we should be encouraging exercise, especially like so many meetings, like 90% of the participants aren't saying anything, right.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们应该鼓励运动，特别是很多会议，有 90% 的参与者什么都不说，对吧。

sentences.en: So if you've got a stationary bike or an elliptical or even like a – I've heard of these little like walking,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一台固定自行车或椭圆机，甚至像——我听说过这种小型散步机，

sentences.en: like un-electric walking treadmills that are just like you start walking and then the belt starts moving.
sentences.zh: 就像那种非电动的步行跑步机，只要你开始走路，履带就会开始动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: It is tough because I like to take minutes in pretty much every meeting that I'm running.
sentences.zh: 这确实有点难，因为我喜欢在我主持的几乎每次会议上做会议记录。

sentences.en: And those are the meetings that I have to control over the schedule.
sentences.zh: 而那些正是我能控制日程安排的会议。

sentences.en: So it is a little bit tricky, but maybe I'll try – maybe I'll try like AI transcriptions or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以这稍微有点棘手，不过也许我会尝试——也许我会尝试用 AI 转录或类似的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, and you know what?
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We should have had – I just realized we should have had this recording session an hour later because right after this, I'm going to pick up my chiming clock.
sentences.zh: 我们本应该——我刚刚意识到我们本该把这次录音推迟一个小时，因为录完这个之后，我要去取我的报时钟。

sentences.en: It's going to drive you crazy.
sentences.zh: 它会把你逼疯的。

sentences.en: That is now finally prepared.
sentences.zh: 它现在终于修好了。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's a future several hundred episodes where Henry the clock – or is it Henri the clock?
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，在未来的几百期节目里，钟表亨利（Henry the clock）——或者叫亨利（Henri the clock）？

sentences.en: Henri the clock, yeah.
sentences.zh: 钟表亨利（Henri the clock），对。

sentences.en: He will make his debut.
sentences.zh: 他将首次亮相。

sentences.en: Anyways, we've got some things to chat about.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们有些事情要聊。

sentences.en: We do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We mentioned the ISO C++ committee meeting in St. Louis, which –
sentences.zh: 我们提到了在圣路易斯的 ISO C++ 委员会会议，这——

sentences.en: Yeah, reflection, baby.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，反射，宝贝。

sentences.en: You want to give a recap on – we'll call this episode – it'll be – well, moving get mentioned, we're not sure, but we'll call it, you know, the St. Louis ISO committee meeting.
sentences.zh: 你想回顾一下吗——我们把这期节目叫做——这将是——好吧，搬家可能会被提及，我们还不确定，但我们暂且叫它，圣路易斯 ISO 委员会会议。

sentences.en: I think, Connor, I – you know,
sentences.zh: 我想，康纳，我——你知道的，

sentences.en: I'm such a boisterous and brash character that you – it would be a huge mistake to not include some of the little content where I'm just having a bad week.
sentences.zh: 我是个如此喧闹狂妄的角色，如果你不把那些我正经历倒霉周的小内容剪进去，那将是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: We're just like I'm cursed.
sentences.zh: 就像我被诅咒了一样。

sentences.en: Like I feel like the listener deserves to do that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得听众有权看到这些。

sentences.en: That's all staying in the episode.

sentences.en: Give us the update about the ISO committee meeting.
sentences.zh: 给我们更新一下 ISO 委员会会议的情况吧。

sentences.en: Well, two big things, I guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想有两件大事。

sentences.en: First is that we voted senders, the C++ Asynchrony Framework, into C++26.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们投票通过将 Senders（C++ 异步框架）纳入 C++26 标准。

sentences.en: And the second is that we design-approved reflection for C++26.
sentences.zh: 第二是我们设计批准了 C++26 的反射功能。

sentences.en: And both of those are pretty big features.
sentences.zh: 这两项都是非常重大的特性。

sentences.en: I mean, I think reflection is a much bigger deal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得反射的影响力要大得多。

sentences.en: Reflection is a huge game-changing feature.
sentences.zh: 反射是一个巨大的、改变游戏规则的特性。

sentences.en: Herb said that he thinks it's going to have the biggest impact on C++ of any feature since C++98.
sentences.zh: Herb 说他认为这是自 C++98 以来对 C++ 影响最大的特性。

sentences.en: I think that's probably fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这评价很中肯。

sentences.en: I think it may compete with a couple others.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它可能会和其他几个特性竞争。

sentences.en: You know, modules impacts the language in ways outside of just the source code, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，模块（Modules）对语言的影响不仅仅是在源代码层面，对吧？

sentences.en: It impacts how we structure code.
sentences.zh: 它影响了我们构建代码的方式。

sentences.en: And it's going to still be years before we sort of see the impact of modules.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还需要几年时间才能真正看到模块带来的影响。

sentences.en: But it's still going to be years?
sentences.zh: 但还需要几年吗？

sentences.en: I think so, because it takes a while for the ecosystem to adopt things.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，因为生态系统采用新事物需要时间。

sentences.en: You could argue that maybe some set of C++11 things have had as big of an impact.
sentences.zh: 你可以争辩说，也许 C++11 的某些特性也有同样大的影响。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know, maybe one could argue move semantics.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不知道，也许有人会说是移动语义（move semantics）。

sentences.en: I'm not even sure I would go that far.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定我会走那么远。

sentences.en: But constexpr may be the thing because it unlocks this whole new field of compile-time metaprogramming.
sentences.zh: 但 constexpr 可能是那个关键，因为它开启了编译时元编程这个全新的领域。

sentences.en: But you could kind of do that before.
sentences.zh: 但你以前其实也能做到那种程度。

sentences.en: Reflection is really very game-changing.
sentences.zh: 反射确实非常具有颠覆性。

sentences.en: It unlocks a variety of things that weren't previously possible.
sentences.zh: 它开启了各种以前无法实现的可能性。

sentences.en: But also, it gives us new ways to evolve the language.
sentences.zh: 而且，它还为我们提供了演进语言的新方法。

sentences.en: Things that we previously had to build as library features we could build.
sentences.zh: 以前我们必须作为语言特性来构建的东西，现在可以作为库特性来构建了。

sentences.en: Or the things we previously had to build as language features, we can now build as library features.
sentences.zh: 或者说，以前必须作为语言特性构建的东西，现在我们可以作为库特性来构建。

sentences.en: Yeah, isn't Spaceship one of those?
sentences.zh: 是啊，Spaceship 操作符不就是其中之一吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, could have done it.
sentences.zh: 是的，本来是可以做到的。

sentences.en: Well, Spaceship had a syntactic component, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，Spaceship 有一个语法组件，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, there was a new operator.
sentences.zh: 比如，有一个新的运算符。

sentences.en: But if you had just decided to call it, like, a member function.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是决定把它称为一个成员函数。

sentences.en: You know, just pick some protocol name.
sentences.zh: 你知道，随便选个协议名称。

sentences.en: You know, like, compare, then you could have done the rest, yeah.
sentences.zh: 比如，compare，那你就可以完成剩下的部分了，是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这很重要。

sentences.en: I'm very confident it'll get in at this point.
sentences.zh: 我现在非常有信心它会被纳入标准。

sentences.en: Our colleague, actually, Andre Alexandroscu, has been working on some follow-on things.
sentences.zh: 我们的同事 Andre Alexandrescu 实际上一直在研究一些后续工作。

sentences.en: Helping to drive some of the injection part of it.
sentences.zh: 帮助推动其中的注入（injection）部分。

sentences.en: How do you put things back in?
sentences.zh: 你如何把东西放回去？

sentences.en: And how do you generate new stuff based on reflection?
sentences.zh: 以及你如何基于反射生成新东西？

sentences.en: You know, how do we generate new functions?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们如何生成新函数？

sentences.en: How do we, like, wrap functions and members and classes?
sentences.zh: 我们如何包装函数、成员和类？

sentences.en: And how do you manipulate the things that you've reflected?
sentences.zh: 以及你如何操作那些已经反射出来的东西？

sentences.en: And the model that we've settled upon is this thing called token sequences.
sentences.zh: 我们最终确定的模型叫做“标记序列”（token sequences）。

sentences.en: So, there's a couple different approaches we explored.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们探索了几种不同的方法。

sentences.en: We explored, like, a spec approach where, like, you could define, like, a new function or type by, you know, you'd call, like, define class.
sentences.zh: 我们探索过一种规范（spec）方法，比如你可以通过调用 define class 来定义一个新函数或类型。

sentences.en: And then you'd pass in this struct that describes all the members of the class and the types and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 然后你传入一个描述类中所有成员、类型之类的结构体。

sentences.en: And we looked into that, too, for functions where you'd define the signature and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我们也研究过函数的情况，你可以定义签名之类的东西。

sentences.en: But one of the properties we wanted is that we wanted when you're writing the injective code, when you're writing new code that's going to be generated at compile time,
sentences.zh: 但我们想要的一个特性是，当我们编写注入代码时，当我们编写要在编译时生成的新代码时，

sentences.en: we wanted it to look like C++ code.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它看起来像 C++ 代码。

sentences.en: And this spec approach doesn't really look like C++ code, and it gets very verbose very faSt.
sentences.zh: 而这种规范方法看起来并不太像 C++ 代码，而且很快就会变得非常冗长。

sentences.en: And there's a couple different variations of that approach.
sentences.zh: 这种方法有几种不同的变体。

sentences.en: There's one that's, I think, in sort of the same broad category, but it's more AST-based, where you're, like, manipulating the AST in a very similar way,
sentences.zh: 有一种我认为属于大致相同的范畴，但更多是基于 AST（抽象语法树）的，你以非常相似的方式操作 AST，

sentences.en: where you're sort of doing it programmatically.
sentences.zh: 也就是以编程方式进行操作。

sentences.en: And I think it had all the same downsides, but it also had the additional downside that exposing up the AST in that way makes it harder to evolve the language.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它有同样的缺点，而且还有一个额外的缺点，即以这种方式暴露 AST 会使语言的演进变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Because, like, you know, for example, if we have our standardized statement expressions, then, like, the AST nodes for expressions might change in type.
sentences.zh: 因为，比如，如果我们有了标准化的语句表达式，那么表达式的 AST 节点类型可能会改变。

sentences.en: They might not be statement nodes, and so it might limit how we'd be able to evolve the language going forward.
sentences.zh: 它们可能不再是语句节点，所以这可能会限制我们未来演进语言的能力。

sentences.en: And then we also looked at, like, a string-based manipulation approach, where the way you injected code is you just, you know, gave it a string and said, here,
sentences.zh: 然后我们还研究了一种基于字符串的操作方法，注入代码的方式就是给它一个字符串，说，给你，

sentences.en: here's some string of C++ stuff, inject this into the program.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些 C++ 代码字符串，把它注入到程序中。

sentences.en: But there were some concerns that that's not really, not going to really be robust, that it could be brittle, that diagnostics could be not great,
sentences.zh: 但有人担心这不够稳健，可能会很脆弱，诊断信息可能不会太好，

sentences.en: that it would sort of not be hygienic.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能不够卫生（hygienic）。

sentences.en: And, you know, you wouldn't get any syntax highlighting underneath that code in the string, which would be a little unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在字符串里的代码下得不到任何语法高亮，这会有点遗憾。

sentences.en: But that was sort of kind of the runner-up approach.
sentences.zh: 但这算是备选方案。

sentences.en: And then the token sequence approach is that instead of manipulating strings, it manipulates these sequences of tokens.
sentences.zh: 然后标记序列方法就是，它不操作字符串，而是操作这些标记序列。

sentences.en: And this is sort of information that pretty much all the compilers carry around.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是所有编译器都会携带的信息。

sentences.en: And so this would be a little bit cleaner.
sentences.zh: 所以这会更干净一些。

sentences.en: And we even imagined that we could build a hygienic macro facility on top of this.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至设想过可以在此基础上构建一个卫生的宏设施。

sentences.en: So in some ways, it's similar to, I think it's somewhat similar to Rust macros and how they work, this token sequence stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些方面，它类似于 Rust 的宏及其工作原理，这种标记序列的东西。

sentences.en: So not clear whether we'll see token sequences in C++26.
sentences.zh: 所以不确定我们是否会在 C++26 中看到标记序列。

sentences.en: It's not part of the core reflection proposal that's been approved.
sentences.zh: 它不是已批准的核心反射提案的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's not even clear how much of injection we'll see in C++26.
sentences.zh: 甚至不清楚我们在 C++26 中能看到多少注入功能。

sentences.en: But we're definitely still working on it.
sentences.zh: 但我们肯定还在研究它。

sentences.en: And we've still got a good bit of time.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还有不少时间。

sentences.en: So we're pretty hopeful that we're going to get some of this follow-on work done.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很有希望完成这些后续工作中的一部分。

sentences.en: We also landed in-place vector at this meeting,
sentences.zh: 我们在这次会议上还通过了 in-place vector（原地向量），

sentences.en: which is a vector which has a fixed capacity where you can just give it a block of memory that's on the stack or statically allocated.
sentences.zh: 这是一种具有固定容量的向量，你可以给它分配一块栈上或静态分配的内存块。

sentences.en: And then it can grow dynamically within that capacity.
sentences.zh: 然后它可以在该容量内动态增长。

sentences.en: It'll never dynamically allocate memory, but it can grow in its size within that fixed capacity.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会动态分配内存，但可以在固定的容量内增加大小。

sentences.en: So that's been something we've been working on for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们一直在研究的东西。

sentences.en: So the std-SIMD proposals made a lot of progress.
sentences.zh: std-SIMD 提案也取得了很大进展。

sentences.en: We're going to likely see that get advanced into C++26 at the next meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会在下次会议上看到它被推进到 C++26 中。

sentences.en: Those are sort of the two big library features that I think we can expect for 26 are going to be SIMD and senders and receivers.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我认为我们可以期待在 C++26 中出现的两个大库特性，即 SIMD 和 Senders/Receivers。

sentences.en: I know that's pretty exciting because std execution and reflection are obviously both big.

sentences.en: I know that I can't remember whose plan it was, but there's some C++26, you know, large plan.

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lot of room.

sentences.en: Wait, there was some time we spent talking about trivial relocation and contracts.
sentences.zh: 等等，我们之前花了一些时间讨论平凡重定位和契约。

sentences.en: It's been another big discussion.

sentences.en: I do not think contracts will make it into C++26.

sentences.zh: 我觉得它可能会进入技术规范（TS）之类的东西。

sentences.en: There's still a lot of open questions there.
sentences.zh: 那里还有很多悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: That's an interesting update because I think the last thing I heard about contracts, because I think, doesn't Teamer, co-host of CppCast, he's, I don't think he's,
sentences.zh: 那是个有趣的更新，因为我记得我最后一次听说契约时，因为我觉得，CppCast 的联合主持人 Teamer，他不，我不认为他，

sentences.en: is he the chair or vice chair?
sentences.zh: 他是主席还是副主席？

sentences.en: If he's not the chair or vice chair, he's one of the regular attendees of that working group.
sentences.zh: 如果他不是主席或副主席，他也是那个工作组的常客之一。

sentences.en: And I think he's been pretty hopeful on the episodes of CppCast when he mentions it, that it'll get in for C++26.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他在 CppCast 的节目中提到它时一直很乐观，觉得它能进入 C++26。

sentences.en: I just think it's unlikely because there's still a lot of uncertainty about the design.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得不太可能，因为设计上还有很多不确定性。

sentences.en: And it would pretty much need to make it at the next meeting or maybe the meeting after that.
sentences.zh: 而且它几乎需要在下次会议或再下一次会议上定下来。

sentences.en: But really, it would need to be settled by the next meeting.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，它需要在下次会议前解决。

sentences.en: Where's the next meeting?
sentences.zh: 下次会议在哪里？

sentences.en: It's in Poland in Wrocław.
sentences.zh: 在波兰的弗罗茨瓦夫。

sentences.en: Who's hosting that?
sentences.zh: 谁主办？

sentences.en: Nokia, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我想是诺基亚。

sentences.en: And my, uh, my Polish girlfriend and my mother will both be, uh, be there.
sentences.zh: 而且我的，呃，我的波兰女友和我母亲都会，呃，会在那里。

sentences.en: That's exciting.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: When is it?
sentences.zh: 是什么时候？

sentences.en: That's, uh, September?
sentences.zh: 那是，呃，九月？

sentences.en: November.
sentences.zh: 十一月。

sentences.en: Why so far?
sentences.zh: 为什么那么晚？

sentences.en: I thought there was three meetings in here.
sentences.zh: 我以为这里有三次会议。

sentences.en: There are, but it's always, um, it's always, um, like February, March, uh, early summer, and then November.
sentences.zh: 确实有，但总是，嗯，总是，嗯，比如二月、三月、呃，初夏，然后是十一月。

sentences.en: And is it in Wrocław or is it in Warsaw?
sentences.zh: 是在弗罗茨瓦夫还是华沙？

sentences.en: No, it's in Wrocław.
sentences.zh: 不，是在弗罗茨瓦夫。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that, is it going to be coinciding with the Code Dive conference?
sentences.zh: 那么，它会和 Code Dive 大会重合吗？

sentences.en: Um, it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: The Code Dive conference is like the, the week after in, in Warsaw.
sentences.zh: Code Dive 大会是在，呃，接下来的一周在华沙。

sentences.en: I don't think I'll actually be able to go to Code Dive this year, unfortunately, because we're going to Core C++.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我觉得我今年可能去不了 Code Dive，因为我们要去参加 Core C++。

sentences.en: Um, and so we'll be, uh, we'll be flying from Warsaw, I think on the 25th.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们，呃，我们会在，呃，从华沙飞走，我想是在 25 号。

sentences.en: Because Core C++ starts on the 26th and, um, uh, Code Dive is on the 25th.
sentences.zh: 因为 Core C++ 在 26 号开始，而，嗯，呃，Code Dive 在 25 号。

sentences.en: So I'm not certain if it's going to work out.
sentences.zh: 所以我不太确定这能不能行得通。

sentences.en: Are you going to meeting C++ as well?
sentences.zh: 你也要去 Meeting C++ 吗？

sentences.en: I am, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，要去。

sentences.en: The one in Berlin?
sentences.zh: 柏林的那场？

sentences.en: I'm going to meet in C++ and I'm doing a little bit of a tour of, uh, German, uh, C++ user groups and HPC centers and people who like GPUs.
sentences.zh: 我要去参加 Meeting C++，并且还要进行一个小巡回，呃，去拜访德国的 C++ 用户组、HPC 中心以及那些喜欢 GPU 的人们。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Well, what, uh, what's the talks that you're going to be given in November?
sentences.zh: 那么，呃，你十一月要做的演讲是什么？

sentences.en: It's going to be my same talk, the Think Parallel talk.
sentences.zh: 还是我原来的那个演讲，关于“思考并行”的演讲。

sentences.en: Um, I'm probably going to give a slightly updated version of it that focuses on some different algorithms than those,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可能会做一个稍微更新的版本，重点关注一些与之前不同的算法，

sentences.en: the scan algorithms that have been in the versions that I've given thus far.
sentences.zh: 也就是我目前为止所给出的版本中包含的扫描算法。

sentences.en: So I may, I may talk about some reduction algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能会，我可能会谈谈一些归约算法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And yeah, and then I guess that full circle, full circle, half a circle, who knows what portion of a circle brings us back to CPP North, uh, which are you giving the,
sentences.zh: 好的，然后我想这兜兜转转，兜兜转转，半个圈，谁知道是圆的哪一部分，把我们带回了 CPP North，呃，你打算做那个，

sentences.en: I think parallel scans talk.
sentences.zh: 我想是并行扫描的演讲。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Cause I was going to say, I've seen the ACC U talks start to come out online.
sentences.zh: 因为我正想说，我已经看到 ACCU 的演讲开始在网上发布了。

sentences.en: I have not seen yours yet because I've been waiting to update the link from whatever episode we included that in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我还没看到你的，因为我一直在等更新链接，从我们在节目笔记中包含该链接的任何一集开始。

sentences.en: And I guess now I have to include it again in this show notes, uh,
sentences.zh: 我想现在我必须再次把它包含在这个节目笔记里了，呃，

sentences.en: but it'll be a, an unlinked link because the, the recording, at least as of yesterday or two days ago, um,
sentences.zh: 但这会是一个无法点击的链接，因为录像，至少截至昨天或两天前，嗯，

sentences.en: is not out yet.
sentences.zh: 还没发布。

sentences.en: Um, but you'll be giving that same talk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你会做同样的演讲。

sentences.en: So I guess, uh, it's good news.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，呃，这是个好消息。

sentences.en: I know they're, I know they're working on it because they asked me if they could give it a longer title because think parallel is not a very good title for SEO.
sentences.zh: 我知道他们，我知道他们正在处理，因为他们问我是否可以给它一个更长的标题，因为“思考并行”这个标题对 SEO 来说不是很好。

sentences.en: And so they wanted, they wanted the YouTube video to have a longer title.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想要，他们想要 YouTube 视频有一个更长的标题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That's an interesting, what are your thoughts on that?
sentences.zh: 那很有趣，你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Because I think my CPP North talk from last year, it's title was composition intuition, but they ended up renaming it, at least in the YouTube video, like, uh,
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得我去年在 CPP North 的演讲，标题是“组合直觉”，但他们最终重命名了它，至少在 YouTube 视频上是这样，比如，呃，

sentences.en: function composition in.
sentences.zh: 函数组合在……

sentences.en: Um, I, I, I, I told them, I, they asked whether they could rename it and I told them that I would prefer not to, because I dislike, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，我，我，我告诉他们，他们问是否可以重命名，我告诉他们我更倾向于不改，因为我不喜欢，嗯，

sentences.en: talks that have a subtitle in the name.
sentences.zh: 名字里带有副标题的演讲。

sentences.en: Um, um, like they wanted to do like think parallel colon, like something, something, something, something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，就像他们想做成“思考并行：冒号，比如某某某某”。

sentences.en: And I just am never a fan of that.
sentences.zh: 我从来都不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: Um, and I think I'm happy to have, you know, some keywords put in the description and, uh, you know, people find it if they're going to find it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我觉得我很乐意在描述中加入一些关键词，呃，你知道，如果人们要找它，自然会找到。

sentences.en: You know, I, I trust the YouTube algorithms, what I'm saying, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我，我信任 YouTube 的算法，我是这么说的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I will say, I will say, oh my God, I, well, a little tangent here, just a small tangent folks.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我会说，我会说，天哪，我，好吧，这里跑题了，只是一个小小的跑题，各位。

sentences.en: I love the YouTube recommendation algorithm, whatever folks, if you're a listener or you're friends of someone that works on the YouTube algorithm, give them a handshake next time.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢 YouTube 的推荐算法，不管是谁，如果你是听众，或者你是 YouTube 算法团队成员的朋友，下次见到他们握个手吧。

sentences.en: Literally with like, I think it was 37 views, the Sean Parent meetup talk from New York C++, which I actually don't know.
sentences.zh: 真的，大概只有 37 次观看，Sean Parent 在纽约 C++ 聚会上的演讲，我其实不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe I am subscribed and that's why, but it was, it was not in my subscription pane.
sentences.zh: 也许我订阅了，这就是原因，但它，它不在我的订阅面板里。

sentences.en: It was on my homepage with the chains talk that we saw back in March.
sentences.zh: 它出现在我的主页上，还有我们在三月份看到的那个链式演讲。

sentences.en: It had 37 views and YouTube recommended that talk to me.
sentences.zh: 它有 37 次观看，而 YouTube 把那个演讲推荐给了我。

sentences.en: Like, let's go.
sentences.zh: 就像是，冲啊。

sentences.en: It's the most esoteric thing.
sentences.zh: 这是最深奥的东西了。

sentences.en: Do you think that YouTube's recommendation algorithm does content analysis?
sentences.zh: 你认为 YouTube 的推荐算法会进行内容分析吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that they recommend solely based on title and description or do you think that they?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们仅仅是基于标题和描述进行推荐，还是你认为他们？

sentences.en: No, they do it because, because the reason I would say that it definitely does content analysis is because when you do a Google search these days,
sentences.zh: 不，他们会这样做，因为，因为我会说它肯定进行了内容分析的原因是，当你现在进行谷歌搜索时，

sentences.en: sometimes it'll give you the timestamp within a YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 有时它会给你 YouTube 视频中的时间戳。

sentences.en: It'll say like minute 337 discusses, like if you say how to, you know, do something, it'll give you a YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 它会说比如第 3 分 37 秒讨论了什么，比如如果你说如何，你知道，做某事，它会给你一个 YouTube 视频。

sentences.en: And then YouTube videos, you can now include chapters in the YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 而且 YouTube 视频现在可以包含章节。

sentences.en: So you can say like minute zero to minute one is the intro minute one to minute three is, you know, some other topic.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说比如第 0 分钟到第 1 分钟是介绍，第 1 分钟到第 3 分钟是，你知道，其他主题。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've ever seen that on a YouTube video, but it might be that, but, but I wonder whether it could just be the keywords too, as well,
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否在 YouTube 视频上见过这个，但这可能是原因，但，但我怀疑这是否也可能只是关键词，

sentences.en: that you attach to YouTube videos, right?
sentences.zh: 你附加到 YouTube 视频上的那些，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, but that wouldn't give you the timestamp.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但这不会给你时间戳。

sentences.en: But I, I, I, I would bet that if they're not doing content analysis for recommendations now, they will, they will be sometime in the, in the near future.
sentences.zh: 但我，我，我，我敢打赌，如果他们现在没有进行内容分析来做推荐，他们很快就会在不久的将来这样做。

sentences.en: You mean, cause they're already doing AI transcription, right?
sentences.zh: 你是说，因为他们已经在做 AI 转录了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They've been doing transcripts for a while now.
sentences.zh: 他们做转录已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: They have, so they, they have the show screen transcript.
sentences.zh: 他们有，所以他们，他们有显示的转录文本。

sentences.en: So that's, that's just text.
sentences.zh: 所以那，那只是文本。

sentences.en: That's pretty low cost for them to, to use in ranking and recommendations, right?
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说在排名和推荐中使用成本相当低，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if, if they're, if they're already doing the thing that, that generates, you know, text from the video, which is the expensive operation, I would assume.
sentences.zh: 就像如果，如果他们已经在做那种，从视频中生成文本的事情，这可是昂贵的操作，我想。

sentences.en: And they're already doing it cause there's already a use case for that transcripts.
sentences.zh: 而且他们已经在做了，因为转录已经有了用例。

sentences.en: Then they've already got that data.
sentences.zh: 那么他们已经有了那些数据。

sentences.en: They may as well use it.
sentences.zh: 他们不妨就用上它。

sentences.en: Um, they're almost certainly already doing, um, like things like sentiment analysis to see, like, to analyze,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们几乎肯定已经在做，嗯，比如情感分析之类的事情，来看看，比如，分析，

sentences.en: like whether somebody is really angry or there's like violence in a video because they have to do that for content moderation, right?
sentences.zh: 比如某人是否真的很生气，或者视频中是否有暴力内容，因为他们必须为了内容审核而这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if someone like uploads a video of like, you know, like crime or like, like stuff like that, or like violence, they, they need to be able to detect that, um,
sentences.zh: 就像如果有人上传了一个视频，比如，你知道，犯罪或者类似的东西，或者暴力，他们，他们需要能够检测到，嗯，

sentences.en: so that they can either moderate it away or that they can put a, you know, graphic violence warning on it.
sentences.zh: 这样他们要么可以将其审核掉，要么可以给它加上一个，你知道，暴力画面警告。

sentences.en: Um, uh, you know, that's, that's probably AI.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，你知道，那，那很可能是 AI。

sentences.en: I mean, it may, maybe there's somebody who just watches all the videos.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可能，也许有人只是在看所有的视频。

sentences.en: I assume some AI is involved.
sentences.zh: 我假设涉及到了某种 AI。

sentences.en: Um, and then they also, they also have to do content analysis for, um, uh, you know, copyright infringement.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后他们还，他们还必须为，嗯，呃，你知道，版权侵权进行内容分析。

sentences.en: Um, uh, so like, like they're already doing a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，所以，就像他们已经在做很多事情了。

sentences.en: I, I'd be, I'd be shocked if they're not feeding, um, uh, like data from, from what you're actually talking about into your, um, into the, uh, the recommendation algorithm.
sentences.zh: 我，我会，我会很震惊如果他们没有把，嗯，呃，比如你实际谈论的数据输入到你的，嗯，输入到，呃，推荐算法中。

sentences.en: So, so maybe the talk title doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以也许演讲标题并不重要。

sentences.en: No, I, I definitely think it does.
sentences.zh: 不，我，我绝对认为很重要。

sentences.en: I mean, talk title and thumbnail, I think are the two most significant things.
sentences.zh: 我是说，演讲标题和缩略图，我认为是两个最重要的因素。

sentences.en: I think for a conference talk, it doesn't matter as much, but I think for like some viral video or just some video where you're trying to get.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于会议演讲来说，它没那么重要，但我觉得对于某些病毒式传播的视频，或者只是你试图获得关注的视频。

sentences.en: But like, I don't, I don't think I need to, I don't think I need to put the word C++ into the title.
sentences.zh: 但就像，我，我不认为我需要，我不认为我需要把“C++”这个词放进标题里。

sentences.en: I mean, as a talk title, you definitely don't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，作为演讲标题，你绝对不需要。

sentences.en: For optimizing on YouTube, I actually don't know.
sentences.zh: 为了在 YouTube 上优化，我其实不知道。

sentences.en: Um, let me put it, would it help?
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我放进去，会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Almost certainly it would help.
sentences.zh: 几乎肯定会有帮助。

sentences.en: Do I think that YouTube, that YouTube's algorithm knows that my talk is about C++, even without me putting a keyword into it?
sentences.zh: 你认为 YouTube，YouTube 的算法知道我的演讲是关于 C++ 的吗，即使我不放关键词进去？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想它知道。

sentences.en: I think it's got some smarts there.
sentences.zh: 我想它在那方面有一些智能。

sentences.en: I think it's done some analysis on the transcripts.
sentences.zh: 我想它已经对转录文本做了一些分析。

sentences.en: I think it's done some rankings and I think it knows this is a thing about C++.
sentences.zh: 我想它已经做了一些排名，而且它知道这是一个关于 C++ 的东西。

sentences.en: And if somebody searches for C++, you know, parallel programming that my talk will come up.
sentences.zh: 如果有人搜索 C++，你知道，并行编程，我的演讲就会出现。

sentences.en: Yeah, like if, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是啊，就像，是啊，完全正确。

sentences.en: Like I'm sure putting code report in my talk title instead of my actual name, because that's what I'm known by on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 就像我肯定在我的演讲标题里放上 Code Report 而不是我的真名，因为那是我在 YouTube 上为人所知的名字。

sentences.en: That would help, but I'm not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 那会有帮助，但我不会那样做。

sentences.en: Although actually, I've seen that one conference actually did.
sentences.zh: 虽然实际上，我见过有一个会议确实这样做了。

sentences.en: They put my name and then they put my handle next to it.
sentences.zh: 他们放了我的名字，然后在旁边放了我的 ID。

sentences.en: But anyways, the name of the talk, they switched composition intuition to function composition in programming languages.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，演讲的名字，他们把“组合直觉”改成了“编程语言中的函数组合”。

sentences.en: Was that a good decision?
sentences.zh: 那是个好的决定吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it is one of the top five talks on the YouTube channel, the CPV North YouTube channel.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它是 CPV North YouTube 频道上排名前五的演讲之一。

sentences.en: So I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe they do know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 也许他们确实知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I, from a, what's the word, like a purity point of view, you know, it upsets me that like it's not the name of the talk, you know,
sentences.zh: 我，从一个，怎么说呢，从纯粹主义的角度来看，你知道，这让我很不爽，因为那不是演讲的名字，你知道，

sentences.en: it's the name of the talk is composition intuition.
sentences.zh: 演讲的名字是“组合直觉”。

sentences.en: And it matches my other talk, algorithm intuition.
sentences.zh: 而且它和我的另一个演讲“算法直觉”很配。

sentences.en: So to change the title in the YouTube thing, you know, what are we doing?
sentences.zh: 所以要在 YouTube 上更改标题，你知道，我们在做什么？

sentences.en: I want to dig into this a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我想深入挖掘一下这个问题。

sentences.en: I want to think about what are the expensive compute workloads in processing a YouTube video.
sentences.zh: 我想思考一下处理 YouTube 视频时昂贵的计算工作负载是什么。

sentences.en: So generating the transcript isn't that bad.
sentences.zh: 所以生成转录并不是那么糟糕。

sentences.en: And I say that because audio data is substantially smaller than video data, right?
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为音频数据比视频数据小得多，对吧？
